about: workflow:keep-tasks-handed-between-anyone: keeps the task records (kind calendar-task) that people, AIs and workflows hand each other, in the person's own store, each write made only when its record is still as it was read. It replaces the records-door writes that the task tools (tool:give-a-task, tool:take-a-task, tool:change-a-task, tool:finish-a-task, tool:see-tasks, tool:see-who-can-take-work) would make (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do): those tools keep the work's rules and answer their writes as keep, and this recipe applies them.

payload.label: Keep the tasks anyone is handed
payload.job: Keep the task records (kind calendar-task) that people, AIs and workflows hand each other in the person's own store, so that each task is taken by exactly one of its assignees and every change of a task is written once, against the task as it was read.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for calendar-task records, proven on the example attempts: a task written only when its id is absent, a change written only when the task is still as it was read (a refused write means it changed), and a batch all or nothing.

source.from: tools/plan-tasks-and-todo-lists (task-moves.mjs and task-moves.json, and the keep list each of its tool rows answers) on trillion-workshop origin/main, read 2026-11-19 CST.
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job: a record, its version, and a write made only when the record is absent or still as it was read, in one transaction. Who may give, take, hand on, finish or withdraw a task, which states it may move through and the stale-take time are the tool's values (task-moves.json), not the store's. A task's assignees are record ids of anyone (a person, an AI, a workflow). The records door and its runner are not used by the keeping; the tool reads its records from input.records and answers its writes as keep.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

tool.description: The tool row to run over the store: tool:give-a-task, tool:see-tasks, tool:take-a-task, tool:change-a-task, tool:finish-a-task or tool:see-who-can-take-work; its input is given as input

input.description: That tool's input, without records (this recipe reads them from the store)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the calendar-task records are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: records (id unique, type, value as a JSON object, version starting at 1 and rising by one with each write). A write is made in one transaction only when the record is absent (expected null) or its current value is the value it was read at (the same JSON); otherwise it is a conflict and nothing changes. A batch makes all its writes, and checks all their conditions, in one transaction; if any conflicts, the whole batch is refused and nothing changes. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway copy of the same kind of store, with the same objects, run the example attempts in order, each through the store's own objects: (1) seed a person person:someone and three AIs ai:north, ai:south and ai:east, each written only if absent (expected null): applied. (2) run tool:give-a-task as person:someone, title "Water the plants", outcome "The plants are watered", assignees [ai:north], key t-one, with the records read from the store as input.records: status written with 1 keep write; apply the keep: applied. (3) the same run again: status written with 0 keep writes. (4) the same key with other words, "Something else": status already-there. (5) tool:take-a-task as ai:north, id record:calendar-task:t-one: taken, applied. (6) tool:change-a-task as ai:north, id t-one, action hand-on, taken_at of the take, assignees [person:someone]: moved true, applied (a person to AI to person handoff). (7) tool:take-a-task as person:someone, id t-one: taken, applied. (8) tool:change-a-task as person:someone, action plan, taken_at of that take, acceptance (outcome, target plant-check:garden, one rule on watered): moved true, applied. (9) tool:finish-a-task as person:someone, id t-one, taken_at, result, summary and check (the same outcome, target and a checked_at within the take): moved true, to Done, applied. (10) tool:give-a-task as person:someone, title "Rename the photos", assignees [] (anyone), key t-two, applied. Two takes of t-two, as ai:north and as ai:south, computed from the same read: applying the first gives applied, applying the second gives conflict and writes nothing. (11) read the store again: tool:take-a-task as ai:south with no id finds nothing to take. (12) tool:give-a-task t-three to ai:east, applied; tool:change-a-task as person:someone, withdraw of t-three (its giver, waiting): moved true, its keep applied. (13) tool:see-who-can-take-work over the store again: ai:north has busy 1. (14) final statuses: t-one Done, t-two In progress with taken_by ai:north, t-three Not needed. The same attempts run in test/keep-tasks-stores.test.mjs (tools/workflows), on PGlite and on a folder of JSON files; both must give these answers.

answers.description: The answer of each attempt, numbered as in the prove step

steps.title: Keep the tasks this run hands
steps.do: Each time the work runs: read the calendar-task records the tool needs from the store (the tasks the call names or lists, and the people and AIs they name) and give them to the tool as input.records; run the tool row over that input; then apply its keep list to the store in order, in one transaction, each write only if its record still has the expected value (null: the record must not exist; a null value removes the record). If a write is refused, the task changed since it was read: read again and decide again with the tool; nothing of that run is kept. Submit each task id written, applied, and each refused write with its id and why.

written.description: Each task id written or applied

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes a calendar-task record; a task that is gone is not taken again. A person, AI or workflow record is removed only by the person's own edit.
